target: _tracker_supersede_lands — a spec-id citation counts only when that spec is done
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: dependent
status: specd
depends_on: 002
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; printf -- '---
id: 002
title: dep
status: built
---
body
' > factory/specs/002-b.md; printf -- '---
id: 003
title: absorbed-it
status: pr-open
---
body
' > factory/specs/003-c.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; tracker_supersede factory/specs/002-b.md me 003 'folded into 003' >/dev/null 2>&1; BEFORE="$(_tracker_unmet factory/specs/001-a.md)"; _tracker_set_field factory/specs/003-c.md status done; AFTER="$(_tracker_unmet factory/specs/001-a.md)"; jq -n --arg b "$BEFORE" --arg a "$AFTER" '{before: $b, after: $a}'
_note: chaining through a spec that has NOT merged yet must not unblock — pr-open is exactly the state tracker.sh's header says does not count, and routing round it via superseded_by would reopen that hole. The same citation starts satisfying the moment 003 actually merges.
